previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex bariatric history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later open reversal and prior gastrostomy tube removal) presented with two days of burning/sharp epigastric abdominal pain with nausea and poor oral intake after recently stopping her home acid-suppressing and mucosal-protective medications. Evaluation showed reassuring labs (including normal lipase), mild transaminase/alkaline phosphatase elevation that improved, and CT abdomen/pelvis without acute findings; abdominal radiograph showed a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern. Her course was notable for orthostatic hypotension with systolic blood pressures into the 80s that improved with IV normal saline and improved intake; AM cortisol was checked and was reassuring. Symptoms improved with scheduled acetaminophen, resumption of pantoprazole, ranitidine, and sucralfate, and an intensified bowel regimen (polyethylene glycol, bisacodyl, docusate, and PRN senna), along with nutrition counseling to use oral supplements. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable with return precautions and medication changes focused on gastritis management and hydration/nutrition.

Brief Hospital Course:
SUMMARY: Ms ___ is a ___ with PMHx laparoscopic RYGB in 
___ (s/p open reversal in ___ who presents with recurrence of 
her abdominal pain, improved with eating, and nausea associated 
with early postprandial filling. She has had several 
hospitalizations for similar abdominal pain. Labs and studies 
were reassuring against acute surgical process or infection. Pt 
was trialed on standing tylenol, a standing bowel regimen, PUD 
medications, avoidance of anticholinergic medications, and a 
non-narcotic pain regimen - which improved her pain. She was 
discharged without narcotics and provided a referral to the 
chronic pain service for presumed postoperative visceral 
hyperalgesia. 

============
ACTIVE ISSUES
============
# ABDOMINAL PAIN: Chronic with multiple hospitalizations for 
similar complaints, likely from visceral hyperalgesia in the 
setting of multiple abdominal surgeries. Last admission the 
recurrence of her abdominal pain was noted to occur 
approximately one month after stopping her home PPI, H2 blocker, 
and Carafate. CT A/P at that time demonstrated no acute 
intra-abdominal pathology. Her pain improved with standing 1g 
Tylenol TID, resumption of pantoprazole/ranitidine/Carafate, 
bowel regimen, and home pain medications and similar 
conservative management was pursued this hospitalization. She 
was evaluated by the bariatric surgery service, who recommended 
no surgical intervention and referral for chronic pain service. 

# Diarrhea: Endorsed diarrhea with negative C. difficile PCR. 
Given absence of other infectious signs, she was treated 
symptomatically with loperamide.
# Diplopia: She reported diplopia, which has been a chronic 
symptom for her. She was evaluated as an outpatient by neurology 
and a EMG was negative for MG. Her pyridostigmine was 
discontinued as this was in process of being tapered and can 
contribute to GI upset. 

===================
CHRONIC/STABLE ISSUES
===================
# H/O SEIZURE DISORDER: Reported. Continued home LevETIRAcetam 
500 mg PO BID 

# DEPRESSION/ANXIETY: Continued home apipirazole and fluoxetine, 
lorazepam and propranolol. 

# INSOMNIA: Continued home zolpidem. 

# S/p RYGB REVERSAL: Continued home MVI, iron. 

# MED REC: Continued home atorvastatin 40mg PO qPM. 

=================
TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
=================

tapered and can contribute to GI upset. Initiated loperamide PRN 
for diarrhea.
